prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Thrips in my plant room😬.

Any suggestions on eradicating them. Yesterday, I began spraying with a solution (70% alcohol / 29% water / 1% peppermint oil). I plan to spray all leaves every week. I have read that this will help control Thrips but not eradicate them. Any advice from people that have overcome thrips?

I have over 80 plants in my plant room and need to aggressively kill this invader. Some of my orchids are over 25 yrs old.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely cause: thrips feeding damage.** The pale, speckled stippling across the leaf, with tiny light flecks, fits thrips. I can't see the insects in the photo, so check for them. Hold a white sheet of paper under a leaf and tap it, or look for tiny dark specks. Thrips frass dots are the clincher, since the frass dots distinguish thrips damage from spider mite stippling, which lacks them. Blue sticky traps will also confirm it. Your plan to treat is right, but the spray needs adjusting.

**Fix, most important first:**

1. **Dilute the alcohol spray much more.** At 70% strength, your mix is too strong for many plants. One guide suggests 1 part rubbing alcohol to 20 parts water as a gentle starting point. Orchids are especially sensitive, so test one leaf first and wait 48 hours. Spray only in the early morning or evening, never in direct sun, and rinse afterward if you see damage. Some guides also warn that sensitive species such as ferns or orchids may show stress at concentrations as low as 2 % ethanol.

2. **Repeat treatment for at least 4–6 weeks, not just once a week for a few sprays.** Eggs sit inside leaf tissue and pupae live in the soil, so stopping when the visible adults disappear is the most common mistake. Use insecticidal soap or spinosad every 5–7 days, covering leaf undersides and new growth. Alternate products to avoid resistance. Soap works best, and do not spray when temperatures are above 90°F or on drought-stressed plants.

3. **Treat the soil too.** Add a neem soil drench, or replace the top layer of potting mix in the worst pots, to reach the pupae.

4. **Isolate and remove.** Move heavily infested plants away from the rest, prune the worst leaves and flowers, and set blue sticky traps. Check every plant, not just the visibly damaged ones. Wait until traps stay clear for about two weeks before calling it over.

Your mix contains peppermint oil, which is not a thrips control on its own, so rely on the steps above.
